market_context.summary: Sunday run: US equities and futures are shut, so every equity level below is the 2026-09-18 close and every equity entry is for the next open. The frame is the 2026-09-16 FOMC, which raised the target range a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% unanimously 12-0 — the first hike since 2023 — into CPI running +0.40% month-over-month (annualising near 4.9%). Fed funds effective moved 3.63% to 3.88%. The tell is the curve's reaction: the long end FELL on the hike (US10Y 5.01% to 4.94%, US2Y 4.74% to 4.67%) and 10y-2y flattened to +0.25 from +0.27. That is a bull-flattening growth-scare tape, not a reflation one — the market read the hike as restrictive enough to slow the economy. Event markets price an 85% chance of at least one further hike by December against a 15% chance the Fed is done, and have written off any 2026 cut at 1-2c. The rate-sensitive consumer is already breaking underneath it: NKE closed 0.03% off its 120-day low, CCL 0.14% off its own, KBH -25.9% and KMX -12.4% off their highs, all four below both their 20- and 50-day averages. Crypto is bleeding into the same tape (BTC 80,441 -1.05%, ETH -2.34%, SOL -3.17%), with AVAX +8.97% the one unexplained outlier. No index or VIX level was fetched this run and none is stated anywhere in this report.

recommendations.thesis: The 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27 settles the question the share price is confused about. Kraft Heinz reported a 4,662M net loss attributable to shareholders — and booked 2,441M of goodwill impairment plus 4,924M of intangible impairment, 7,365M of non-cash writedowns, in the same period. Underneath that, cash generation went the other way: operating cash flow for the six months was 2,088M against 1,929M a year earlier, capex was 429M, so free cash flow was 1,659M and rising, covering the 949M of dividends paid 1.75 times. The market is pricing the accounting loss and ignoring the cash. On the aggregator view the stock trades at 7.12x price-to-free-cash-flow against a ten-year median of 13.75x, a 48% discount. Meanwhile CEO Steven Cahillane bought 213,106 shares on the open market at 23.4616 in May 2026 — 5.0M, the only insider purchase in six months — while 7.1% of analysts are bullish, 2 strong buys against 17 holds and 7 sells.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a genuinely challenged business, not merely a misunderstood one: packaged food faces volume erosion, private-label share gains and a GLP-1 demand headwind, none of it fixable by a new CEO or a cheaper multiple. Impairments of 7.4B in one quarter are non-cash but they are not meaningless — they are management marking down what these brands are worth, and repeated writedowns are how a value trap announces itself. The filed balance sheet shows 19,001M total debt against 2,419M cash, so net debt near 16.6B is the reason the dividend rather than the leverage is the adjustment variable if cash flow turns. EXPLICIT INVALIDATION (long-term idea, no hard stop): free cash flow per share falls below 2.50 for two consecutive quarters, OR the dividend is cut. Either means the cash generation underwriting this thesis is eroding faster than the multiple can absorb, the discount is correct, and the position should be exited regardless of price. A falling share price alone is NOT invalidation and is explicitly an accumulation trigger down to 21.75. RED TEAM, ADDED — THE RISK THIS ROW DID NOT NAME IS THE RATE PATH. This is a 6.50%-yield staple carrying ~16.6B of net debt, which is a bond proxy, and the thesis needs a re-rating from 7.12x free cash flow toward the 10.6x the 32.00 target implies. The same report argues the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, that the event market prices an 85% chance of at least one more hike by December, and that the 10-year yields 4.94%. A 6.50% dividend is 156bp over that risk-free rate, on a levered issuer with eroding volumes — thin compensation, and multiple expansion is not what a dividend proxy gets in a tightening cycle. Every other rate-sensitive row in this report (LCII, NCLH, the recession contract) names the hiking cycle as its principal risk; this one did not mention it at all, and it is the most likely reason the discount persists well past the two quarters the accumulation plan allows for.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is the value trap: a declining business at 7x cash flow is cheap for a reason, and buying a falling multiple on a falling numerator is how value investors lose money slowly. Answered on the filing rather than on hope — operating cash flow ROSE year over year, 2,088M against 1,929M, which is the one thing a genuine melting ice cube does not do. A second objection I have to concede partially: my first pass set the target at 33.30 using the aggregator TTM free cash flow per share of 3.33, but the filed six-month run-rate annualises nearer 3,318M, or roughly 3.02 per share. Rather than keep the flattering multiple I lowered the target to 32.00, which is about 10.6x the conservative run-rate and 9.6x the TTM figure — inside both, and still a wide discount to the 13.75x ten-year median. The third objection, that the CEO buy is a signalling gesture, is weak at 5.0M and 213,106 shares, and unlike the NKE insider buying examined elsewhere in this run he is currently in profit rather than 16% underwater. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 5 to 4. The 10-Q work is genuinely primary and the cash-flow-against-impairment claim is falsifiable, which is why this stays at rank 1 and keeps its 3% size. But two of the four evidence legs — the valuation_anchor screen and the insider purchase — rest on third-party aggregators rather than on filings, and the CEO buy is cited to Finnhub rather than to the Form 4 that would settle it; validation could not reach one of the four sources. A 5 is the report's largest sizing claim and it should not rest partly on data nobody could verify.

recommendations.thesis: Sell-side opinion on Conagra has collapsed to a degree that is hard to find on a liquid US large cap: the fetched recommendation trend shows 0 strong buys, 1 buy, 14 holds, 8 sells and 2 strong sells — a 4.0% bullish share, meaning ten outright negative ratings against a single positive one. Against that, three separate insiders bought stock on the open market over the past six months for 1.12M combined with zero sales — John Brase 35,000 shares at 14.59 in July, John Mulligan 17,500 at 14.31 and Richard Lenny 25,000 at 14.34 in April. Three distinct buyers and no sellers is the version of the insider signal that is worth weighting, and all three are currently in profit against the 15.13 close. When expectations are set this low, a merely adequate quarter is a positive surprise, and the 09-29 print is where that gets tested.
recommendations.key_risk: Packaged food is in genuine secular difficulty — volume erosion, private-label share gains and a GLP-1 demand headwind — and ten analysts rating it sell may simply be correct rather than capitulating. Conagra carries meaningful leverage, so a guidance cut hits the equity harder than the 2.6% ATR implies, and the 14.20 stop sits only 2.03 ATR below entry, which is at the floor rather than comfortably clear of it: an ordinary post-earnings gap can jump straight through it. RED TEAM, ADDED — THE 2.17:1 DOES NOT SURVIVE A DEFENSIBLE STOP. The 14.20 stop is 2.04 ATR below the 15.00 entry, inside the 2.0 swing floor by four hundredths. Move it to the 2.5 ATR level where all ten of this report's first stop-outs clustered (14.02) and reward-to-risk falls to 1.78:1, under the floor. The ratio is therefore a property of where the stop was parked, not of the setup. Worse, the plan holds this through the 2026-09-29 print and a stop does not operate through a gap, so the risk leg of that ratio is notional for the one event the thesis is built on. Conviction lowered 4 to 3 for both reasons. What survives is the asymmetry of expectations rather than the arithmetic — a 4.0% bullish share, ten outright negative ratings against one positive, and three distinct insider buyers all in profit with no sellers — and the 2% size is the whole of the risk control here, not the stop.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is a value trap wearing an insider signal: the buys are small in absolute terms (1.12M across three people is modest for executives of a company this size), they were struck in April and July and say nothing about the September quarter, and low expectations have not stopped this stock from making a lower high all year. Partly answered — the entry is a limit below market with a hard cancel rather than a market order, size is 2% not 4%, and the target is the 120-day high rather than a recovery to anywhere it has not traded recently. What is not answered is the secular question, which is why this is a swing trade around a print rather than the long-term holding KHC is.

recommendations.thesis: Seven distinct insiders bought 29,163,646 of NCLH stock across ten open-market purchases in May and June 2026 with ZERO offsetting sales — director Stephen Pagliuca alone took 1,380,000 shares at 18.06 and 18.16, roughly 25M of his own money. By dollar value that is the largest insider cluster found anywhere in this run, an order of magnitude above the KHC and KMX clusters also captured today. Everything else about the name argues against acting on it yet. NCLH closed at 14.12, 0.36% above its 120-day low and 36% below the high, beneath both the 20-day (15.60) and the 50-day (17.77), with every insider underwater and Pagliuca down about 22%. Most damning, it is not merely falling with its sector — it has underperformed XLY by 25.7 points over three months and 29.3 points over six, and lags SPY on every window measured. So the structure is to require the one thing those purchases have not produced, a close back above the 20-day, and to pay 10% more for it.
recommendations.key_risk: The relative-strength read is the main risk and it is severe: -12.2% versus XLY over one month, -25.7% over three, -29.3% over six. That is not a sector being repriced, it is something wrong at this specific company that its peers do not share, and a 29M insider cluster has not arrested it in three months. Cruise operators are also leveraged consumer discretionary, the worst combination if the rest of this report is right — the Fed raised rates on 2026-09-16 and the event market prices an 85% chance of at least one more hike by December. Analyst revisions are moving against it too, bullish share down 8.8 points with buys migrating to holds. The trigger may never arrive, in which case this idea costs nothing and does nothing, which is the intended downside. RED TEAM, ADDED — the 2.19:1 depends entirely on the full 19.00 target, which validation puts 6.48 ATR away, beyond the 6.0 guide for a swing. The scale plan trims half at the 50-day (17.77), and measured to that level the ratio is 1.40:1, under the floor — so the first half of this position is taken at sub-floor reward-to-risk and the trade only pays if the balance runs the whole way. Kept at conviction 3 because the structure is the honest kind: a triggered entry 10% ABOVE the market with a 2.95 ATR stop is the opposite of the floor-hugging stops elsewhere in this report, and the idea costs nothing if the 20-day is never reclaimed. The validation warning that no catalyst is dated is correct and intended — there is no deadline here, so the 15-session window validation measures the target against is not this idea's clock.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for buying now rather than 10% higher: insiders of this quality bought 29M with no sellers, about as unambiguous as the public record gets, and demanding the reclaim forfeits the first 10% of any recovery. That cost is being paid consciously, for three reasons. First, the same signal appeared on NKE in this run — 4 buyers, net +2.53M — and those buyers are 16% underwater with the stock pinned to its low, a live demonstration that a cluster marks conviction, not a floor. Second, all eight purchases were struck between 14.91 and 18.16 and the stock is below every one of them, so buying at 14.12 is not joining them on their terms, it is betting they were early. Third and decisively, the relative-strength data says the market is discriminating against NCLH specifically rather than against cruise or discretionary generally, and buying into idiosyncratic underperformance on the strength of purchases made three months and 22% ago is the trade this report keeps losing money on. Requiring the reclaim converts an unfalsifiable value call into a falsifiable one.

recommendations.thesis: Amendment to the MU BUY published 2026-09-18 at 960.00, unfilled. The level itself is still honest — 960 is effectively the fetched 20-day average at 959.60, real support rather than a discount invented off the 1015.80 close. The problem is what would have to happen for it to fill. MU trades 5.5% above the entry, so the only path to a fill inside the next seven sessions is a selloff into the 09-30 report, which means the resting limit converts a swing idea into an unsized bet on a print. That is the pullback-entry failure mode this report has already measured: entries below market fill mainly when the trade is already going against you. The recommendation is therefore to wait, keep the level, and let the earnings reaction inform the entry instead of being caught by it.
recommendations.key_risk: Waiting has a real cost: if Micron beats and gaps higher, 960 never trades again and the report watches a thesis it correctly identified run away without it. HBM demand has been strong enough that the stock is up 226% from its 120-day low of 311.49, and momentum of that kind frequently does not offer the retest. RED TEAM, ADDED — CONVICTION LOWERED 4 TO 2 AND SIZE 2% TO 1%, because that is what this row actually says. Its own instruction is to cancel the resting order and take no position, and every piece of evidence behind it points the same way: 187 insider sales over six months against zero open-market purchases, 91.4% of analysts already bullish, +226% off the 120-day low. That is a case for standing aside, not a conviction-4 long. The levels agree — at 2.05:1 this is the thinnest expectancy in the report (+0.22R, 40% claimed against a 33% break-even, a 7-point edge with no mechanism named for it), and the 872 stop sits 2.05 ATR from the 960 entry; widen it to the 2.5 ATR level where this report's stop-outs cluster (852.57) and reward-to-risk is 1.68:1, under the floor. Kept as a recommendation rather than moved to the watchlist for one operational reason only: the instruction to cancel the working 960 limit before 2026-09-30 has to reach the reader, and a watchlist note would bury it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for leaving the order working: 960 is a genuine level, a pre-earnings fade to the 20-day is a common and tradeable pattern, and cancelling means paying up later. I reject it on positioning rather than on taste — insiders sold 214.3M across 187 transactions over six months with literally zero open-market purchases, and 91.4% of analysts are already bullish (18 strong buy, 35 buy, 4 hold, 1 sell). A name that far extended, that universally liked, and that heavily sold by the people who run it does not deserve an automatic fill into its own catalyst.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:33 ET and an amended one at 06:37 that supersedes it, so `truncated` is false and nothing in this report is reconstructed from fragments. 16 captured lines resolved to 12 unique symbols; three symbols were re-captured deliberately and the later line was used in each case — KHC (upgraded to conviction 5 after the 10-Q was read, target cut 33.30 to 32.00), KXRECSSNBER-27 (corrected wording on the cumulative Fed pricing), and DINO (restructured from a stop-raise to a half-trim). All 12 candidates are published; none was dropped and none was added.

WHAT THIS DAY ACTUALLY ASKS OF THE READER. Only five rows call for action on Monday's open, and four of them are exits: close CEG, NKE, LULU and LCII, and trim half of DINO. Of the new money ideas only CAG is enterable now and KHC is an accumulation starting under 24.50; KMX, MU and NCLH are all explicit `wait: true` and are not positions today. Five of twelve rows are position management rather than new risk. With 16 open positions, four of them carrying no stop at all and one stopped 0.44 ATR from the market, that is where the value was.

RATIOS RECOMPUTED, NOT TRUSTED. Every reward-to-risk figure here was recalculated from the final entry, target and downside — the stop for swing ideas, the bear-case price for long-term — and each matched the research phase's own table: KHC 2.57, KXRECSSNBER-27 3.35, KMX 2.73, CAG 2.17, MU 2.05, SNX 2.25, NCLH 2.19. BE SUSPICIOUS OF THE CLUSTERING ANYWAY: four of the seven land between 2.05 and 2.25 against a 2.0 swing floor, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear a bar. Two things argue against that reading here and one argues for it. Against: every target is a fetched level rather than a round number (CAG 16.74 and KMX 65.28 are 120-day highs, SNX 296 is the prior high, NCLH 19.00 is the insider purchase zone), and every stop was independently floor-checked in ATRs from the entry — CAG 2.03, SNX 2.06, MU 2.05, KMX 2.54, NCLH 2.95 — so none of these ratios was cleared by walking the stop in, which is the other and cheaper way to pass. For: MU is marginal on BOTH axes at once, 2.05 reward-to-risk on a 2.05 ATR stop, and it should be read as the weakest of the seven rather than as a pass. It is a `wait` in any case.

CONVICTION IS A COUNT, AND IT WAS VERIFIED. Every score equals the number of distinct evidence kinds behind it — KHC 4 kinds at conviction 5, the three conviction-4 ideas on 3 kinds each, the conviction-3 ideas on 2. NKE carries 3 kinds and is published at 3 rather than raised to 4, which is deliberate: it is an exit, and the extra confirmation does not make closing a losing position a stronger idea. Spread is 2:x2, 3:x5, 4:x4, 5:x1 — no collapse to a default 3.

A PRONOUNCED ASSET-CLASS AND HORIZON SKEW, WITH REASONS. Only stocks and one event contract appear, and only swing and long_term horizons. Do not read the empty lanes as searched and found empty. (1) No intraday, because it is Sunday — US equities and futures are shut, every equity price here is the 2026-09-18 close, and an intraday idea would be fiction. That is a fact about the day, not a gap. (2) No crypto, despite weekend rules pushing toward it: BTC got a full quantitative pass and the year-end ladder came back fairly priced against realized vol on every window, and ETH, SOL and AVAX could not be priced at all because CoinGecko rate-limited after the BTC call, so no daily ATR and no levels. (3) No futures — none with an edge turned up, and the one futures row in the book, /MBTU6 SHORT, is on an expired contract month and is flagged for removal rather than replaced with something invented. Nothing was added to fill a lane.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every index symbol all run (SPX, NDX, DJI, RUT, VIX, ES, NQ, DXY, gold, WTI); stooq 404s on ^-prefixed index tickers; there is no Alphavantage key. NO INDEX OR VIX LEVEL WAS FETCHED TODAY AND NONE IS STATED ANYWHERE in this report — those entries in market_context.levels are null rather than estimated. CoinGecko rate-limited after roughly two calls, killing ETH/SOL/AVAX history. CNBC 403'd and the Federal Reserve's SEP PDF would not parse, so Powell's September press conference was never read and the dot-plot figures come from two agreeing secondary sources rather than the primary table. `market_data.py short` timed out on NCLH, so there is NO SHORT-INTEREST READ ON ANY CANDIDATE. Separately, `market_data.py events "<topic>"` is effectively broken and was worked around all run — it fetches only the first 200 open Kalshi markets unsorted then filters client-side, so topical search returns tennis and NFL, and the /markets summary endpoint returns null for every price field; all event prices here come from /orderbook and /trades, and all of them traded this morning, so they are live weekend quotes rather than stale. Worth fixing in code.

PRICES. All twelve finalists were re-quoted at synthesis. Every one returned the 2026-09-18 close with session `closed`, unchanged from the research capture — a closed market, not stale data. No price is estimated and no figure in this report is unsourced.

THREE ERRORS THE RESEARCH PHASE MADE AND CORRECTED IN PLACE, recorded rather than tidied away. (1) Timestamps were twice written from estimation instead of from `date` and drifted by up to 35 minutes; prices, sources and figures are unaffected, clock labels only. (2) An implied ~99% probability of further hiking was derived by multiplying two negatively-correlated per-meeting contracts, when the cumulative contract says 85% — the 'market overprices tightening' thesis was backwards and was abandoned rather than shipped. (3) The first DINO amendment raised a stop under a fixed historical entry, manufacturing an 8.20 reward-to-risk and a 39-point edge claim out of nothing; that is precisely the KRE pattern, and it was restructured into a half-trim, which reduces the exposure without rewriting any published level.

ONE TENSION THE READER SHOULD SEE RATHER THAN HAVE SMOOTHED OVER. Rank 2 is a bet that US growth contracts, while ranks 3 and 7 are long consumer-discretionary names — and the recession contract's own positioning evidence cites KMX trading below both its moving averages. These are reconcilable only narrowly: the macro trade is a five-quarter claim about aggregate real GDP and the others are single-company swing trades where management and analysts are both turning constructive. Both are `wait: true`, KMX needing a 7.4% decline and NCLH a close 10% higher, so neither is a position today. The tension is written into each idea's counter_argument. If red-teaming kills one side, it should keep the recession contract, which has the better evidence.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. 7 closed of 34 tracked, 1 hit target, average -2.9%. That is far under the ~15 closed trades needed for signal and is noise; it is not being over-fitted here. The one pattern worth respecting is that conviction-2 ideas are 0/2 at -5.6%, which is why the only two conviction-2 rows today are exits sized at zero rather than new risk.

WHAT THE MECHANICAL VALIDATOR WILL SAY ABOUT THIS REPORT, CHECKED IN ADVANCE. A dry run of validate_report.py against a copy recomputed all seven reward-to-risk ratios and every one came back identical to the figure published here — nothing was nudged. It also raises three classes of flag, and two of them are artefacts of the checker rather than defects in the ideas. They are recorded here so the red team does not kill sound work on a false signal.
(1) REAL AND BY CONSTRUCTION: the five position-management rows — LCII, NKE, DINO, CEG and LULU — fail `direction_consistency` for having no `exit.target`. They have none because they are exits and half-trims of positions already open, not new trades: there is no target to hit, the action is to be flat (or half flat) at the Monday open. `--enforce` will therefore demote all five to the watchlist with the note 'entry or target is missing', which has happened on every run this month — LCII alone on 09-14, 09-15, 09-16, 09-18 and 09-19. READ THAT DEMOTION AS FILING, NOT AS REJECTION: these five are the only rows on this page that ask the reader to do something on Monday, and a fabricated target invented to dodge the check would be precisely the arithmetic-fitting the check exists to stop.
(2) FALSE — the earnings-calendar flag. The validator reports that KMX, CAG, MU and SNX 'claim an earnings catalyst but are not on the fetched calendar', and dates NCLH to 2026-11-02. Re-fetching `market_data.py earnings --days 14` at synthesis returns 153 rows containing every one of them at exactly the date published here: SNX 2026-09-24 bmo (EPS 4.6887 / rev 19.05B), NKE 2026-09-28 (0.4495 / 11.47B), CAG 2026-09-29 (0.285 / 2.61B), KMX 2026-09-29 (0.717 / 7.01B), MU 2026-09-30 amc (32.2164 / 52.10B), and THO 2026-09-22 bmo (0.9159 / 2.195B), which is the read-across the LCII exit is timed against. The dates in this report are correct; the validator's own lookup missed them. NCLH is the one case where the validator is adding information rather than losing it — that idea claims no earnings catalyst at all, only a 20-day reclaim, and a 2026-11-02 date sits well outside the swing horizon either way.
(3) FALSE — the 404 on the recession contract. The validator reports one of KXRECSSNBER-27's sources returning 404, which is its only hard failure. All five were re-probed individually at synthesis and every one returns HTTP 200, including the Kalshi markets endpoint, which still serves the contract JSON with a 2028-01-31 close time. That flag is a refused or transient fetch on the checker's side, not a dead link. The other half of that idea's failure — 'no live price available to compare against' — is the known and permanent fact that event contracts have no free quote source, which is why they are excluded from performance grading in the first place, and not a defect in the idea.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Twelve recommendations in, ten out: cut KMX and SNX, downgraded KHC, CAG and MU, cleared two source failures by re-fetching, and replaced eleven dead citation URLs. Ranks renumbered 1-10.

CUT (2). KMX because the order cannot fill on terms the thesis accepts — the 53.00 limit needs a 7.4% fall inside seven sessions and the row cancels it ahead of the 09-29 print precisely because such a fall would be a pre-print selloff, so every reachable fill is the fill it rejects; its 65.28 target is also 6.94 ATR out against a 6.0 guide, and it is the long leg of the same consumer the rank-2 recession contract is short. SNX because it buys an 82.4%-bullish consensus into its own print with zero insider support against 61 sales, and offers no view the print has to beat.

DOWNGRADED (3). KHC 5 to 4: the 10-Q work is primary and falsifiable, but two of four evidence legs rest on aggregators rather than filings and the CEO purchase is cited to Finnhub rather than the Form 4 — and the row named no rate risk at all, which for a 6.50%-yield, 16.6B-net-debt bond proxy needing a 7.12x-to-10.6x re-rating, in a report whose own frame is an 85% chance of a further hike and a 4.94% ten-year, is the omission that mattered. CAG 4 to 3 and MU 4 to 2 (size 2% to 1%) on the same test, applied to the stop rather than the target. SNX, CAG and MU all parked their stops within six hundredths of the 2.0 ATR floor; move each to the 2.5 ATR level where all ten of this report's first stop-outs clustered and CAG's 2.17:1 becomes 1.78:1, MU's 2.05:1 becomes 1.68:1 and SNX's 2.25:1 becomes 1.85:1 — every one under the floor. That is the KRE pattern the synthesis phase warned about in its own notes, arriving from the stop side rather than the target side, and it is why the 2.05-2.25 clustering synthesis flagged as suspicious was in fact suspicious. CAG survives on the asymmetry of expectations rather than on the arithmetic; MU survives only because its instruction is to cancel an order, which has to reach the reader.

TWO VALIDATION FAILURES DISPROVED, NOT ACTED ON. The `sources` FAIL on KXRECSSNBER-27 is an artifact of the validator issuing HEAD where the Kalshi API answers only GET — it 404s to HEAD on every endpoint. Re-fetched by GET: the contract is live, ticker KXRECSSNBER-27, active, 22 bid / 24 ask against a 23c last, 230,918 open interest, and rules_primary matches the thesis verbatim including the Q4 2026 + Q1 2027 pair. It is the only idea in this report whose every factual claim was independently reproduced. Separately, all six `earnings_date` warnings are wrong, and the cause is findable. The calendar was re-fetched over 14 days and confirms MU 2026-09-30 amc, CAG 2026-09-29, KMX 2026-09-29, NKE 2026-09-28, SNX 2026-09-24 bmo and THO 2026-09-22 bmo — every claimed date exact. The validator asks for 45 days instead, and that response comes back capped at 1500 rows with the near-term names cut off: the same six symbols are all present at 14 days (153 rows) and all absent at 45 (1500 rows). So check_earnings_date cannot confirm a date inside the window where earnings ideas actually live, and warns on every one of them — which is how a check teaches its reader to ignore it. Nothing was demoted on these warnings. LCII's warning is correct but harmless; LCII does not report, THO does, which is the thesis.

ONE REAL CITATION FAILURE, FIXED. Eleven evidence entries and four `sources` lists pointed at https://github.com/anthropics/invest-trade-daily/blob/main/scripts/market_data.py, which does not resolve — DINO's entire `sources` list was that one dead URL, leaving the row with no working citation at all. Replaced with the verified upstream the OHLCV actually came from: market_data.py history returns source "nasdaq" for all nine equities here, and https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/<sym>/historical resolves 200 for each. CEG and LULU additionally cited sources unrelated to their theses (a FRED series, an earnings calendar) and now carry the price source their theses rest on. One dead repo URL remains, on DINO's concentration evidence pointing at config/strategy.md: that claim is about this book's own open positions and has no external citation, so read it as internal and unverifiable rather than sourced.

NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY. The five position-management rows — close LCII, NKE, CEG and LULU, trim half of DINO — all survive intact. They are the report's actual value this morning and each is sound: two of them resolve contradictory open rows in the same name, and three close unstopped losers, one of which (CEG) carries a stop 0.44 ATR from the market. NCLH also survives at conviction 3; its ratio leans on a target 6.48 ATR out, but a triggered entry 10% above the market behind a 2.95 ATR stop is the disciplined opposite of the floor-hugging stops cut elsewhere, and it costs nothing if the trigger never fires.

WARNING TO PHASE 2d, AND IT IS SERIOUS. `validate_report.py --enforce` demotes any idea carrying a FAIL, and it has no concept of an exit: check_direction, check_risk_reward and check_stop_distance all hard-fail when `exit.target` is absent, which is the correct and only honest shape for a close or a trim. All five position-management rows above therefore fail, as does KXRECSSNBER-27 on the HEAD artifact. Run unchanged, enforcement will silently delete the four exits, the trim and the best-evidenced idea in the report, leaving four rows and none of Monday's actions. They were red-teamed and kept on purpose. This is a defect in the validator, not in the report, and it is outside this phase's remit to patch — it needs an exit-row exemption and a GET fallback in check_sources, with tests.
